claims.text: The initial cast refractory multi-principal element alloy, exemplified by NbMoTaWVTi, has limited ductility and a coarse grain structure.
Mo and Re are gamma-partitioning elements.
Minor Mo and Re additions produce negative lattice misfit and promote N-type rafting.
Minor Mo and Re additions provide solid-solution strengthening.
Severe plastic deformation at intermediate strain rates can refine the target refractory alloy to a grain size below 50 nm.
A controlled low-temperature anneal will stabilize the nanocrystalline structure.
The combined alloying, deformation, and annealing route will produce a stable FCC+BCC solid-solution structure without brittle intermetallics.
Very high processing speeds around or above 1800 rpm can generate a bimodal grain distribution.
Increasing rotational speed to 1800 rpm substantially lowers the high-angle grain-boundary fraction relative to lower-speed processing.
Negative lattice misfit caused by Mo and Re stabilizes the target alloy against phase separation and brittle intermetallic formation.
Entropy stabilization and kinetic suppression of diffusion maintain the FCC+BCC dual-phase structure.
Replacing V with Fe in a W-Ta-Cr-V-based alloy promotes undesired intermetallic phases rather than a single-phase solid solution.
Grain refinement and TiO precipitation can substantially increase compressive yield strength in NbMoTaWVTi relative to its as-cast state.
The proposed nanocrystalline dual-phase structure will significantly enhance hardness.
The proposed alloy will retain ductility superior to alloys with coarse brittle intermetallics or bimodal grain structures.
At sufficiently high temperature, diffusion and surface-energy minimization can cause Au and Cu phase separation in high-entropy nanoalloys despite entropy-based solid-solution stabilization.
Annealing above the rapid-grain-growth threshold destabilizes the proposed nanocrystalline microstructure.
An annealing interval exists that relieves residual stress without permitting precipitate coarsening.
SPD retains high-angle grain boundaries that contribute to the proposed nanocrystalline structure.
Brittle Laves phases generally deteriorate plasticity.

contradictions.description: The mechanism affirmatively attributes dual-phase stability to thermodynamic stabilization from lattice misfit, whereas the uncertainty field states that it is unknown whether the structure is thermodynamically stable or merely kinetically trapped.
